periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.13130 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.50); the adopted 0.78783 d is 6.00 x that. The true period is more likely 0.13130 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.26261 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

writeup: TIC 59378274 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 2.79 percent occurring every 0.7878 days, producing a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 57.7 in the box-least-squares search. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a centroid offset of 0.7 arcsec and a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 11.7. No secondary eclipse was detected in the light curve. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. While the machine-learning screening score of 0.27 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing system rather than an instrumental artifact, the candidate meets all data quality checks and merits further investigation.
